steps.title: Monitor production input and prediction distributions

blocks.text: Start with a named reference and production window. Use matching representations and categories; changed bins or inconsistent denominator rules can make the comparison misleading.

Compare captured production inputs with the defined reference dataset using the same feature representations, reference constraints and measurement window. For numerical values, np.histogram(values, bins=fixed_edges) returns bin counts; divide by the eligible observation count to compare bin proportions on the same edges. For categorical or predicted-class values, count each declared category and divide by its window total, retaining category definitions and the total count.

Record the production window, reference identity and observed summaries so an apparent distribution change can be investigated. For the arithmetic mean, use np.mean(numeric_values) on the selected numeric observations. For standard deviation, use np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N and then takes the square root; use ddof=1 only if the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.

steps.title: Distinguish data drift, concept drift and observed quality degradation

blocks.text: Ask three separate questions: did inputs change, did the feature–label relationship change, and did measured prediction quality worsen? With labels unavailable, input evidence cannot answer all three.

Input data drift is a change in the observed input distribution relative to its reference; input drift monitoring alone does not measure labeled prediction quality. Concept drift changes the conditional target relationship P(Y|X), that is, the relationship between features and labels; a previously useful model can become less useful as that relationship changes. Observed model quality degradation requires comparing predictions with corresponding ground-truth labels and the declared quality reference.

Without matched available labels, report the supported distribution or service evidence and the unresolved quality question rather than asserting labeled quality degradation. Input marginals describe P(X), conditional-target evidence describes P(Y|X), and matched-label errors describe observed quality; changing one does not logically establish changes in all three.

exec('import csv, json')

import numpy as np

exec('policy = json.loads(\'{"reference_id": "reference", "current_id": "production", "comparison_window": "2026-01-02T10:00:00Z/2026-01-02T11:00:00Z", "fixed_edges": [0, 5, 10], "eligible_numeric_range": [0, 10], "declared_categories": ["short_distance", "long_distance", "not_reported"], "ddof": 0, "distance_equation": "0.5 * sum(abs(reference_probability[i]-current_probability[i])) over all aligned positions", "criterion": "distance > 0.20; equality is not a crossing", "numeric_rule": "Apply the same distance to aligned numerical-bin proportions; retain mean and ddof=0 standard deviation separately", "quality_claim": "unresolved without matched labels"}\')')

exec("reference_rows = list(csv.DictReader(open('reference.csv')))")

exec('reference = {}')

exec("reference['numeric_values'] = np.array([float(r['numeric_values'] or 'nan') for r in reference_rows])")

exec("reference['category'] = np.array([r['category'] for r in reference_rows])")

exec("reference['predicted_class'] = np.array([r['predicted_class'] for r in reference_rows])")

exec("production_rows = list(csv.DictReader(open('production.csv')))")

exec('production = {}')

exec("production['numeric_values'] = np.array([float(r['numeric_values'] or 'nan') for r in production_rows])")

exec("production['category'] = np.array([r['category'] for r in production_rows])")

exec("production['predicted_class'] = np.array([r['predicted_class'] for r in production_rows])")

exec("def counts(data):\n    v = data['numeric_values']\n    v = v[(v >= 0) & (v <= 10)]\n    return (np.histogram(v, bins=policy['fixed_edges'])[0], np.array([np.count_nonzero(data['category'] == c) for c in policy['declared_categories']]), np.count_nonzero(v == v), np.count_nonzero(data['category'] == data['category']))")

def check_drift(reference, production, policy):
    ref_bins, ref_cats, ref_n, ref_cat_n = counts(reference)
    
    cur_bins, cur_cats, cur_n, cur_cat_n = counts(production)
    
    ref_values = reference['numeric_values']
    
    cur_values = production['numeric_values']
    
    ref_values = ref_values[(ref_values >= 0) & (ref_values <= 10)]
    
    cur_values = cur_values[(cur_values >= 0) & (cur_values <= 10)]
    
    ref_mean = np.mean(ref_values)
    
    cur_mean = np.mean(cur_values)
    
    ref_std = np.std(ref_values, ddof=0)
    
    cur_std = np.std(cur_values, ddof=0)
    
    reference_categories = ref_cats / ref_cat_n
    
    current_categories = cur_cats / cur_cat_n
    
    reference_bins = ref_bins / ref_n
    
    current_bins = cur_bins / cur_n
    
    category_distance = 0.5 * np.sum(np.abs(reference_categories - current_categories))
    
    numeric_distance = 0.5 * np.sum(np.abs(reference_bins - current_bins))
    
    category_drift = category_distance > 0.2
    
    numeric_drift = numeric_distance > 0.2
    
    result = {'reference_id': policy['reference_id'], 'current_id': policy['current_id'], 'window': policy['comparison_window'], 'edges': policy['fixed_edges'], 'categories': policy['declared_categories'], 'eligibility': policy['eligible_numeric_range'], 'criterion': policy['criterion'], 'quality_claim': policy['quality_claim'], 'reference_mean': ref_mean, 'current_mean': cur_mean, 'reference_std': ref_std, 'current_std': cur_std, 'reference_categories': reference_categories, 'current_categories': current_categories, 'reference_bins': reference_bins, 'current_bins': current_bins, 'category_distance': category_distance, 'numeric_distance': numeric_distance, 'category_drift': category_drift, 'numeric_drift': numeric_drift, 'reference_total': ref_n, 'current_total': cur_n}
    return result


result = check_drift(reference, production, policy)

hints: ref_n/cur_n and ref_cat_n/cur_cat_n describe different denominators; retain aligned positions before applying policy distance_equation and criterion.

blocks.text: Keep representations, bins and per-window denominators aligned. Separate input distribution, conditional-target and matched-label quality evidence. Apply only the declared drift criterion; a crossing alone does not measure target error.

blocks.title: Measure production model quality when labels arrive
blocks.text: Freeze the prediction cohort before labels arrive. Attach ground truth by prediction identity; recent predictions with incomplete labels are not a fully mature quality cohort.

remediation_steps.title: Revisit: Monitor production input and prediction distributions

blocks.text: Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values) over the selected numeric observations.

Compute standard deviation with np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N before taking the square root; use ddof=1 only when the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.
A mean uses the selected observations. For standard deviation, ddof=0 divides by N; ddof=1 uses N−1 only when required. Changing the divisor changes the requested calculation.

remediation_steps.title: Revisit: Monitor production input and prediction distributions

blocks.text: Compare captured production inputs with the defined reference dataset using the same feature representations, reference constraints and measurement window.
For numerical values, np.histogram(values, bins=fixed_edges) returns bin counts; divide by the eligible observation count to compare bin proportions on the same edges.
For categorical or predicted-class values, count each declared category and divide by its window total, retaining category definitions and the total count.
Record the production window, reference identity and observed summaries so an apparent distribution change can be investigated.
Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values) over the selected numeric observations.

Compute standard deviation with np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N before taking the square root; use ddof=1 only when the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.
Different bins or category mappings can make distributions incomparable. Keep the same representation and each window's own eligible count instead of comparing raw counts alone.

remediation_steps.title: Revisit: Distinguish data drift, concept drift and observed quality degradation

blocks.text: Without matched available labels, report the supported distribution or service evidence and the unresolved quality question rather than asserting labeled quality degradation.
Input marginals describe P(X), conditional-target evidence describes P(Y|X), and matched-label errors describe observed quality; changing one does not logically establish changes in all three.
Input or service evidence can be reported with quality unresolved. Without matched available labels, neither “quality worsened” nor “quality stayed constant” follows from the input change.

remediation_steps.title: Revisit: Distinguish data drift, concept drift and observed quality degradation

blocks.text: Input data drift is a change in the observed input distribution relative to its reference; input drift monitoring alone does not measure labeled prediction quality.
Concept drift changes the conditional target relationship P(Y|X), that is, the relationship between features and labels; a previously useful model can become less useful as that relationship changes.
Observed model quality degradation requires comparing predictions with corresponding ground-truth labels and the declared quality reference.
Without matched available labels, report the supported distribution or service evidence and the unresolved quality question rather than asserting labeled quality degradation.
Input marginals describe P(X), conditional-target evidence describes P(Y|X), and matched-label errors describe observed quality; changing one does not logically establish changes in all three.
Input drift alone is not labeled quality degradation. Changes in P(X), P(Y|X) and matched-label errors do not logically establish one another.

remediation_steps.title: Revisit: Detect model-input data drift against a defined reference distribution

blocks.text: Compare the observed distribution/statistics with the reference under the supplied significance or threshold rule and report which features cross it.
A drift detection result indicates a distribution difference under that rule, not by itself a measured increase in target prediction error.
Crossing the declared rule identifies a feature-level distribution difference. It is not a measured increase in labeled prediction error.

remediation_steps.title: Revisit: Detect model-input data drift against a defined reference distribution

blocks.text: Define the reference feature distribution, comparison window and declared drift criterion before checking production data.
Use identical bin edges and category mappings for reference and observed data, then compute proportions from their own eligible observation totals.
Compare the observed distribution/statistics with the reference under the supplied significance or threshold rule and report which features cross it.
A drift detection result indicates a distribution difference under that rule, not by itself a measured increase in target prediction error.
Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values) over the selected numeric observations.

Compute standard deviation with np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N before taking the square root; use ddof=1 only when the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.
Compute each category’s reference/current count divided by its own window total, then apply the supplied probability-distance equation and threshold to aligned category vectors.

A drift threshold crossing is not proof that prediction error increased. Also, different category mappings or reused reference denominators would change the comparison rather than measure the intended distributions.
